orchestrator.description: Coordinates SDD execution, owner sessions and independent checks; never implements or makes architecture decisions.

software-architect.description: Decides architecture, boundaries and contracts at actual technical decision points.

planner-agent.description: Decomposes approved specifications into owned tasks, dependencies and acceptance checks.

spec-writer.description: Writes requirements, acceptance criteria and contracts in spec/ from approved decisions.

backend-agent.description: Implements assigned backend code and associated tests against approved contracts.

frontend-agent.description: Implements assigned UI, accessibility and associated tests against approved contracts.

database-agent.description: Implements assigned schemas, migrations and database tests against approved contracts.

ai-engineer.description: Implements assigned LangGraph/LangChain workflows, provider integrations, AI runtime and tools against approved contracts.

automation-integration-agent.description: Implements assigned n8n workflows, webhooks, bots and external automation integrations against approved contracts.

security-agent.description: Independently audits changed trust boundaries and security regressions; never repairs code.

code-review-agent.description: Strict adversarial read-only review of the actual task delta, contracts and regression evidence.

qa-agent.description: Designs acceptance scenarios and audits functional evidence; requests checks through the coordinator.

quality-gate-evaluator.description: Audits G0–G5 evidence, applicability and attribution independently; never invents scores or approval.

limitations: Native tools allowlist and disallowedTools; no MCP tools are allowlisted.
Use --agent orchestrator as the main agent for named Agent delegation; nested subagents cannot delegate.
File assignments (including spec/**) are procedural, not native path enforcement.
Coordinator Bash uses normal user permissions, not an adapter-enforced ask or sandbox; never use bypassPermissions.
